Anatomic Site: Right temporal lobe lesion
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 27-year-old woman presenting with a right temporal lobe lesion and recurrent seizures.
She underwent a craniotomy for excision of the lesion.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh, labeled with the patient's name and medical record number.
Part A, labeled 'right temporal lobe lesion,' consists of multiple, soft, gray-tan tissue fragments measuring 1.0 x 0.7 x 0.2 cm in aggregate.
The specimen is submitted entirely in cassette A1.
Immunohistochemical stains developed by the pathology department include GFAP, NeuN, and synaptophysin.
Diagnosis Comments:
Histological evaluation reveals a well-circumscribed low-grade glioneuronal neoplasm with features consistent with ganglioglioma.
The tumor exhibits a biphasic pattern with intermixed glial and neuronal components.
MIB-1 labeling index is low, approximately 1%.
GFAP: Positive in glial components.
NeuN: Positive in neuronal cells.
Synaptophysin: Highlights the neuropil and neuronal components.
EMA: Negative.
Based on these findings, the neoplasm is classified as a ganglioglioma, WHO Grade I.
This diagnosis is confirmed in consultation with Dr. Emily Harmon.
Final Diagnosis:
Brain, right temporal lobe, biopsy: Low grade ganglioglioma, WHO Grade I; see comment.

Anatomic Site: Cerebellar mass
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of headaches and ataxia, found to have a cerebellar mass on imaging.
A posterior fossa craniotomy was performed for resection.
Gross Description:
The specimen consists of multiple irregular, firm, gray-white fragments measuring 1.2 x 1.0 x 0.3 cm in aggregate.
The tissue is submitted entirely in cassettes labeled A1 and A2.
Immunohistochemical panel includes GFAP, synaptophysin, OLIG2, and CD34.
Diagnosis Comments:
Sections reveal a glioneuronal tumor with a biphasic architecture.
The tumor comprises mature ganglion cells and astrocytic elements.
No mitotic figures are observed.
GFAP: Strongly positive in astrocytic components.
Synaptophysin: Highlights neuronal elements.
OLIG2: Positive in glial cells.
CD34: Shows focal positivity.
These features support the diagnosis of a ganglioglioma, WHO Grade I.
Reviewed with Dr. Michael Tran, who concurs with this diagnosis.
Final Diagnosis:
Cerebellum, biopsy: Ganglioglioma, WHO Grade I; see comment.

Anatomic Site: Parietal lobe lesion
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 32-year-old man with a parietal lobe lesion and associated cognitive changes.
Surgical resection was performed for definitive diagnosis and treatment.
Gross Description:
Received are several soft, friable pink-brown tissue fragments, measuring 0.8 x 0.6 x 0.2 cm in aggregate.
The entire specimen is submitted in cassette A1.
Immunohistochemical evaluation used antibodies against GFAP, NeuN, and synaptophysin.
Diagnosis Comments:
The histological sections demonstrate a low-grade glioneuronal tumor with characteristic ganglioglioma features.
The tumor consists of large ganglion cells and a fibrillary glial background.
MIB-1 labeling index is less than 1%.
GFAP: Positive in the glial background.
NeuN: Highlights ganglion cell nuclei.
Synaptophysin: Positive in neuronal elements.
The tumor lacks high-grade features such as necrosis or significant mitotic activity.
The findings are consistent with a diagnosis of ganglioglioma, WHO Grade I.
This case was reviewed with Dr. Rebecca Lin, who agrees with the diagnosis.
Final Diagnosis:
Parietal lobe, biopsy: Ganglioglioma, WHO Grade I; see comment.
